question.text: The locus of a point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>z</mi></math> represented by the equation <math><mfenced close="|" open="|" separators="|"><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mo>|</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>|</mo></math> on the argand plane is (where, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>z</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><msqrt><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></msqrt></math>)

options.text: an ellipse with foci at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn></math> and <math><mo>–</mo><mi>i</mi></math>
a line passing through the origin
a circle on the line joining <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn></math> and <math><mo>–</mo><mi>i</mi></math> as diameter

solution.text:
Given, z-1=z-i

⇒  z lies on the perpendicular bisector of the line joining (1, 0) and (0, 1) and it is a straight line passing through the origin.
